subject: music
topicDisplay: Area of Study 4: Popular Music 1980 to Present
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In house and dance music, a steady bass drum sounding on every beat of the bar is known as what?
questions.explain: A 'four-to-the-floor' pattern places the bass drum on all four beats, driving the pulse of dance music.

questions.q: Which piece of music technology stores short recorded sounds so they can be replayed and manipulated?
questions.explain: A sampler records and stores audio clips that can be triggered, pitched and looped in a track.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation MIDI stand for?
questions.explain: MIDI is a standard protocol allowing electronic instruments and computers to communicate performance data.

questions.q: A short, catchy melodic or rhythmic pattern that is repeated, often on guitar or keyboard, is called a what?
questions.explain: A riff is a repeated pattern that helps give a pop or rock song its identity.

questions.q: What term describes the most memorable, catchy part of a pop song designed to stick in the listener's mind?
questions.explain: The hook is the instantly memorable idea, often found in the chorus, that 'hooks' the listener.

questions.q: Power chords, built from just the root and fifth, are most characteristic of which style?
questions.explain: Power chords played on a distorted electric guitar are a defining sound of rock music.

questions.q: Computer software used to record, edit, arrange and mix music is known as a what?
questions.explain: A DAW is the central software environment in which modern popular music is produced.

questions.q: An electronic device that produces and sequences programmed percussion sounds is a what?
questions.explain: Drum machines generate and pattern electronic percussion, central to much 1980s and dance music.

questions.q: Auto-Tune is a production tool most commonly used to do what?
options: Correct or alter the pitch of a vocal
Increase the overall tempo of a track
Add distortion to an electric guitar
Widen the stereo image of the drums
questions.explain: Auto-Tune adjusts vocal pitch, either subtly to fix tuning or as an obvious stylistic effect.

questions.q: Adding reverb to a vocal recording mainly creates the impression of what?
options: The sound being performed in a large space
questions.explain: Reverb simulates the natural reflections of a room, giving a sense of space and depth.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a middle 8 (bridge) in a pop song?
options: To provide contrast to the verse and chorus
To repeat the main hook unchanged
To open the song before the intro
To fade the song out at the end
questions.explain: The middle 8 introduces new material, offering variety before the final choruses.

questions.q: Early 1980s synth-pop is characterised chiefly by its heavy use of which instruments?
questions.explain: Synth-pop built its sound around electronic keyboards and programmed drums rather than acoustic instruments.

questions.q: In music production, 'looping' refers to what?
options: Repeating a section of recorded audio continuously
Removing all reverb from a track
questions.explain: Looping repeats a chosen segment, a technique underpinning much dance and hip-hop production.

questions.q: In verse-chorus form, how do the verse and chorus typically differ?
options: The verse usually has changing lyrics while the chorus repeats the same words and music
Both always have identical lyrics and melody
The chorus changes each time while the verse repeats unchanged
Neither the verse nor the chorus is ever repeated
questions.explain: Verses advance the story with new lyrics, while the chorus returns with the same memorable material.

questions.q: Sampling, a technique strongly associated with hip-hop, involves producers doing what?
options: Incorporating sections of pre-existing recordings into a new track
Performing entirely live with no recording
Notating all parts by hand on paper
questions.explain: Sampling reuses fragments of earlier recordings, layering them to build a new piece.

questions.q: Multi-track recording allows a producer to do what?
options: Record different instruments on separate tracks and mix them independently
Play only one instrument at a time with no overdubs
Produce music without using any microphones
Remove the need for a chorus section
questions.explain: Multi-tracking captures parts separately so each can be balanced, edited and processed on its own.

questions.q: A section of a song returns three times with exactly the same tune and words, each time featuring the main hook. Which section is this?
questions.explain: The repeated section carrying the hook and unchanging lyrics is the chorus.

questions.q: A producer wants a singer's voice to repeat as fading echoes in time with the beat. Which effect should they use?
questions.explain: Delay creates timed, fading repeats of a sound, producing rhythmic echoes.

questions.q: A dance track is built on a two-bar bass pattern that is repeated unchanged throughout. This repeating pattern is best described as what?
questions.explain: A continually repeated musical pattern such as this bassline is called an ostinato.

questions.q: A track features a steady bass drum on all four beats, a tempo around 120-130 bpm and repeated electronic loops. Which genre does this most suggest?
questions.explain: The four-to-the-floor pulse, tempo and electronic loops are hallmarks of house and dance music.
